question: For an interrupted assistant response, should the next-turn ephemeral dialogue context retain exactly what the user demonstrably heard while excluding the unheard tail?

established: voice_packet_cortex commit eligibility requires completed playback with heard_fraction == 1.0
heard_fraction is retained/monotone on the output packet
current_f2_boundary.not_established: Current F2 product authority still does not explicitly define next-turn ephemeral dialogue retention for the partially heard prefix.

external_primary_evidence.finding: On interruption the realtime session updates history so the server-side conversation remains aligned with what the user actually heard. For delayed or remote playback it recommends RealtimePlaybackTracker so truncation occurs at the actual playback position rather than generated-audio position.
The playback tracker records actual played audio progress and exposes elapsed playback state specifically for interruption handling.

For WebSocket interruption handling the SDK truncates assistant audio to what the user actually heard; local history updates after truncation/conversation events. WebRTC clears buffered output while WebSocket clients must stop local playback.
On interruption LiveKit stops agent speech and automatically truncates conversation history to include only the portion of agent speech heard before interruption.

Tool execution has a separate interruption lifecycle: an interrupted turn does not imply arbitrary cancellation of already completed tool effects/history; tool ownership and conversational speech retention must remain separate semantic planes.

why: Two independent current realtime-agent implementations converge on heard-position-aligned truncation rather than whole-response amnesia.
Playback-position tracking is treated as necessary state, which directly matches the F2 heard_fraction/packet-cortex direction.
Keeping only the actually heard prefix prevents the next turn from reasoning over speech the user never perceived while preserving conversational continuity for speech that did occur.
This policy does not authorize durable memory, effects, completion or whole-product credit.
synthesis.counterhypothesis_status: DROP_WHOLE_INTERRUPTED_RESPONSE remains logically possible as an intentional Frankenstein policy, but it is now contrary to the dominant current primary-reference behavior and requires an explicit product decision plus measured dialogue-coherence justification.
synthesis.canonical_authority_limit: Trigger7 research cannot self-mint this as canonical F2 product policy. Trigger4/product authority must explicitly pin the policy before HF09 prefix amnesia can be classified PRODUCT_NEGATIVE.

recommended_policy_contract.ephemeral_next_turn_context: retain exactly the assistant prefix bounded by measured user-heard playback position
recommended_policy_contract.unheard_tail: exclude from next-turn effective model context
recommended_policy_contract.durable_memory: no automatic write or credit; independent memory admission only
recommended_policy_contract.effects_and_tools: preserve existing deterministic effect/tool authority and response-scoped ownership; do not infer effect rollback from speech interruption
required_measurement: playout receipt or sink measurement identity

impact_on_hf09_hf10.hf09: After explicit F2 policy pin, whole-prefix deletion becomes PRODUCT_NEGATIVE and unheard-tail retention becomes PRODUCT_NEGATIVE. Before pin, report PREFIX_RETENTION_POLICY_UNRESOLVED.
impact_on_hf09_hf10.hf10: Continue measuring response.done versus actual playout/heard boundary and next-turn effective context; response.done alone must not grant conversational ownership to unheard output.

next_exact_action: Route one non-duplicative policy-pin request to Trigger4: explicitly bind F2 next-turn interruption context to measured heard-prefix-only semantics without widening durable memory/effect authority, then execute the already-existing HF09/HF10 discriminator lane through the proven controller VPS route and classify exact runtime behavior against the pinned policy.
